chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, raising it, said:

Indeed, al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) went out from the bathhouse, and a man came across him, so he said, 'May your istihmamuk (bathing) be good.' He said, 'O dimwit, and what are you doing with the 'ist' here?' He said, 'May your hameemuk (perspiration) be good.' He said, 'Do you not know that al-hameem is the perspiration?' He said, 'May your hammamuk (bathhouse) be good.' He said, 'And when my hammam is good, so what is for me? But say, 'May it be purified what is good from you, and may it be good what is purified from you.'

key_terms.الاسْتِحْمَام: The act of bathing (using the ist- prefix)
key_terms.لُكَع: Dimwit / Simpleton (term of endearment or mild rebuke)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning behind Imam al-Hasan's explanation of 'hameem' in the bathhouse hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s mastery of Arabic morphology and semantics, using the root 'ḥ-m-m' to distinguish between the heat of the bathhouse and the sweat of the body. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on linguistic precision in religious etiquette, transforming a casual greeting into a lesson on purity (taharah) and the spiritual state of the individual. The exchange underscores the importance of mindful speech, where words are chosen to reflect both physical cleanliness and inner virtue.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, and Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Nahawandy, from Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary, raising it, said,

‘Al-Hassanasws Bin Aliasws went out from the bathhouse, a person came across himasws, so he said, ‘May yourasws Istihmamuk be good’. So heasws said: ‘O dimwit, and are you doing with utilising the ‘ist’ over here (in the word)?’ So he said, ‘May your Hameemuk be good’. So heasws said: ‘But do you not know that Al-Hameem is the perspiration?’ He said, ‘May your Hamaamuk be good’. Heasws said: ‘And when myasws bathing is good, so which thing is for measws, but say, ‘May it be purified what is good from youasws, and may it be good what is purified from youasws’.
en.sarwar: 20. Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu‘ manner has narrated the following from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan: “Once we in a group of our people entered a bathhouse and when coming out we met abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who asked us, ‘Wherefrom are you coming?’ We replied, ‘We are coming from the bathhouse.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘May Allah make your bathing pure and clean.’ We then said, ‘We pray to Allah to keep our souls in service for your cause.’ We then went with him (the Imam). He (the Imam) entered the bathhouse and we waited until he came out, then we said, ‘May Allah make your bathing pure and clean.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘May Allah cleanse you.’”
